label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 1.74, a PHQ-9 depression mean of 1.75, and a notably high GAD-7 anxiety mean of 2.17, these respondents consistently score above moderate thresholds across all three psychological distress measures. Their extensive screen time may both reflect and reinforce patterns of social isolation and emotional difficulty.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Extended daily screen time (more than 5 hours)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting compounded emotional distress

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They score well below typical thresholds on all three psychological distress measures, suggesting generally positive mental health and social connectedness.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77 on normalized scale)
Moderate and controlled daily screen or internet usage (1–3 hours)
Pattern consistent with stable social support and emotional regulation

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the affective distress typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of emotional resilience or effective coping that buffers against clinical mood and anxiety difficulties.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level education or above, with moderate daily screen/internet use of 1–3 hours
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating frequent feelings of social disconnection
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) suggesting minimal mood impairment
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) indicating limited worry or nervousness
Moderate internet/screen engagement (1–3 hours daily), neither highly connected nor fully disengaged
Possible reliance on internal coping strategies that decouple loneliness from clinical distress
tone: Quietly isolated yet psychologically stable; socially understimulated rather than emotionally overwhelmed
